player.linkText: How does this system work? Read the Player Guide
player.title: Player Guide
player.subtitle: Everything you need to know about submitting your minister application.
player.whatIsBody: This system automates SVS minister assignments. Instead of manually coordinating with R4s, you submit your available speedups and preferred time slots. The system then assigns minister positions based on your contribution level and availability, ensuring the highest contributors get priority.
player.step1Fid: Enter your Player ID (FID) — this is your unique identifier found in your game profile. You will need it later to view your assignment or make updates.
player.step1Alliance: Enter your Alliance Tag (required, up to 3 characters).
player.step1Speedups: Enter your speedup totals in DAYS for each category: Construction, Research, Troop Training.
player.step1General: If you plan to use General Speedups toward Construction or Research, add those days into the respective totals instead of the General field.
player.step2Select: You will see a separate time grid for each SVS day: Construction (Monday), Research (Tuesday or Friday), and Troop Training (Thursday).
player.step2Days: Select ALL hours you are available — the more times you select, the better your chance of being assigned a slot.
player.step2Timezone: Use the timezone dropdown to view and select times in your local timezone. Times are stored in UTC behind the scenes.
player.step2Tolerance: Your actual assignment may be ±20 minutes from your chosen hour (e.g., selecting 05:00 could mean a 04:50 or 05:20 slot).
player.step3Body: Review all your information and time selections, then submit. You can always come back and update later using your FID.
player.heatmapBody: The time grid uses color coding to show how many other players have applied for each time slot:
player.heatmapTip: Tip: Choosing less competitive (blue) time slots increases your chance of being assigned.
player.updateBody1: From the minister page, click "Apply or update":
player.updateStep1: Enter your FID on step 1 and click "Next".
player.updateStep2: Your current assignments for all three days will be shown at the top (or "None" if not yet assigned).
player.updateStep3: The wizard opens with your saved answers already filled in. Step through it and change anything — speedups, time preferences, alliance, etc.
player.updateStep4: Click "Update" on the last step (Review & Confirm) to save your changes.
player.updateNote: Assignments shown here are subject to change until confirmed in-game. Check back frequently.
player.assignmentsBody: Here is how the system decides who gets assigned and when:
player.assignmentsPoint1: Points are calculated from your speedups and fire crystals. Higher contribution = higher priority.
player.assignmentsPoint2: The system assigns slots in 30-minute increments across the day.
player.assignmentsPoint3: Players with the most points are assigned first to their preferred time slots.
player.assignmentsPoint4: If all your preferred times are taken by higher-ranked players, you may appear as "unassigned" and an admin will work to fit you in.
player.timezoneBody: All times are stored in UTC (Coordinated Universal Time). When filling out the form or viewing your assignments, use the timezone selector to convert times to your local timezone. The system remembers your selection. If you see a time like "05:00 UTC" and you are in UTC+3, that is 08:00 your time.
player.tip1: Select as many time slots as you honestly can — the more flexible you are, the better your chance of getting assigned.
player.tip2: Enter your speedups accurately — inflating numbers does not help and admins can verify.
player.tip3: Check the heat map to find less competitive slots if you have flexibility.
player.tip4: Come back to "Apply or update" regularly to check if you have been assigned.
player.tip5: If your availability changes, update your submission right away — do not wait until the last minute.
player.roundsNote: Each minister round is a new application. Your profile is remembered, but speedups and times start blank: click "Use my last answers" to copy them from your previous round.

admin.title: Admin Guide
admin.subtitle: Complete guide to managing players, assignments, and publishing schedules.
admin.overviewBody: The admin dashboard has three main tabs: Players, Assignments, and Settings. The Players tab lets you view, edit, delete, and export/import player data. The Assignments tab lets you auto-assign minister slots, manually adjust with drag-and-drop, lock assignments, publish schedules, and export to Excel. The Settings tab controls system-wide options including state number, application closing time, research day, and fire crystal field visibility.
admin.playersView1: All submitted players appear in a sortable table with their game name, alliance, speedups, and calculated points.
admin.playersView2: Click any column header to sort (e.g., sort by Construction days to see top contributors).
admin.playersView3: Use the search bar to find specific players by name or FID.
admin.playersView4: Fire crystal columns can be shown or hidden via the "Show Fire Crystal Fields" toggle in the Settings tab.
admin.playersEdit1: Click the Edit button on any player row to modify their information.
admin.playersEdit2: You can change their speedups, alliance, name, or any other field.
admin.playersEdit3: Click Save to apply changes. The points will recalculate automatically.
admin.playersDeleteBody: Click Delete on a player to remove their application from this round (with confirmation). To start over for the next event, use "Start new round": it closes the current round without deleting anything, and past rounds stay viewable (read-only). Use Export first if you want a file backup.
admin.exportBody: Click the green "Export Players" button to download all player data as a JSON file. This serves as a backup that you can restore from later. The file includes all player fields, speedups, and time preferences.
admin.importBody: Click "Import Players" and select a previously exported JSON file. The system matches players by FID — existing players get updated, new FIDs get created. This is useful for restoring data or migrating between systems.
admin.autoAssign1: Select a day tab (Monday, Tuesday/Friday, Thursday) and click "Auto Assign".
admin.autoAssign2: The system calculates points for all players, then assigns highest-point players first to their preferred time slots.
admin.autoAssign3: Each time slot gets one 30-minute assignment. Players who cannot fit appear in the "Unassigned" section.
admin.autoAssign4: You can run auto-assign multiple times — it will not disturb locked (sticky) assignments.
admin.dragDrop1: Drag any player card from one time slot to another to manually reassign them.
admin.dragDrop2: Drag a player to the "Unassigned" area to remove them from the schedule.
admin.dragDrop3: Changes save automatically when you drop a player into a new position.
admin.sticky1: When you manually place a player into a slot, they are automatically locked (shown with an amber highlight and lock icon).
admin.sticky2: Locked players are preserved when you re-run auto-assign — they will not be moved.
admin.sticky3: Click the lock icon on any player to toggle their lock status.
admin.sticky4: Use this to protect specific assignments (e.g., a key player at a critical time) while letting auto-assign handle the rest.
admin.researchDayBody: Research day can be either Tuesday or Friday depending on your state's SVS schedule. Toggle this in the **Settings tab** — it affects which day label appears and which player time preferences are used for research assignments.
admin.settingsBody: The Settings tab has the global state number, plus the selected round's own settings (each round keeps its own):
admin.settingsState: State Number — Sets which state number appears in the welcome message on the home page.
admin.settingsClosing: Application Closing Time — Set a deadline for new applications. After this time, new players cannot submit but existing players can still update. The home page shows a countdown and grays out the submit button when closed.
admin.settingsResearch: Research Day — Toggle between Tuesday and Friday for research day assignments.
admin.settingsFireCrystals: Show Fire Crystal Fields — When enabled, fire crystal input fields appear on submission forms and admin tables.
admin.publishBody: After finalizing assignments, publish the schedule so players can see it:
admin.publish1: Click "Publish Schedule" on each day tab you want to make visible.
admin.publish2: Published days show as clickable links on the home page for all players.
admin.publish3: Click "Unpublish" to hide a day's schedule if you need to make further changes.
admin.excelBody: Click "Export to Excel" to download a spreadsheet with all assignments:
admin.excel1: The workbook contains a tab for each day (Monday, Tuesday/Friday, Thursday) plus an "Unassigned" tab.
admin.excel2: Each tab shows time slots, assigned player names, alliances, and point totals.
admin.excel3: Use this for record-keeping or sharing with other R4s who don't have admin access.
admin.workflow1: Configure the Settings tab — set your state number and application closing time.
admin.workflow2: Wait for players to submit their applications (share the link in state chat).
admin.workflow3: Review the Players tab — check for suspicious data or missing info.
admin.workflow4: Go to Assignments tab and run Auto Assign for each day.
admin.workflow5: Review the results — manually drag-drop to fix any issues.
admin.workflow6: Lock any manually-placed assignments you want to protect.
admin.workflow7: Export to Excel for your records.
admin.workflow8: Publish each day's schedule when ready — players will see it on the home page.

tyrantAdmin.subtitle: How to run Frost Dragon Tyrant sign-ups: rounds, time windows, stats and exports.
tyrantAdmin.overviewBody: The Frost Dragon Tyrant admin has two tabs. Players shows the sign-ups of the selected round: stats, breakdowns and a table you can search, filter, sort, export and clean up. Settings holds the round's time windows and closing time. Use the event switch at the top to move between events without logging in again.
tyrantAdmin.rounds1: Each Tyrant event is a round. The round selector shows the current round by default; pick an older one to look back at it.
tyrantAdmin.rounds2: "Start new round" closes the current round and opens a new one with the name you choose (and an optional closing time). Nothing is deleted.
tyrantAdmin.rounds3: The new round copies the time windows of the previous one. Players start a fresh sign-up and can press "Use my last answers".
tyrantAdmin.rounds4: Past rounds are read-only: you can view and export them, but not change them.
tyrantAdmin.windowsBody: On the Settings tab you set the time windows (UTC) that players can pick in this round:
tyrantAdmin.windows1: Change a window's start and end time; the end must be after the start.
tyrantAdmin.windows2: Tick "Opening Rush" on the windows that count as the opening rush (shown first, with their time).
tyrantAdmin.windows3: Add a window (up to 12) or remove one. "Reset to defaults" brings back the standard windows from 11:01 to 18:00.
tyrantAdmin.windows4: Press "Save windows" to apply. Changes affect this round only; players who already chose a removed window keep it on their sign-up.
tyrantAdmin.closingBody: Set a closing time on the Settings tab (or when you start a round). After it, new players cannot sign up, but players who already did can still edit their sign-up. Press Clear to remove the deadline.
tyrantAdmin.statsBody: The top of the Players tab sums up the round:
tyrantAdmin.stats1: Cards: total players (and "of N" when filtered), players available for the opening rush, Discord VC and number of alliances.
tyrantAdmin.stats2: Troops: for each troop type the camp level counts (FC10 ... FC1, old pre-FC values as stored, none) and the tier counts (T11 ... T8, none). Below: players per time window, roles wanted and alliances.
tyrantAdmin.stats3: Every count is a button: tap it to filter by it (tap again to remove). All stats are recalculated for the filtered players.
tyrantAdmin.filters1: Search by in-game name, FID or Discord ID.
tyrantAdmin.filters2: The filter bar: alliance (several allowed), time windows or "Opening rush", troop type (or all three) with "camp at least" and tier (T10 or better / T11 only). "More filters" adds furnace, power, gems, Discord VC, roles (any or all) and submitted date.
tyrantAdmin.filters3: Click a column header to sort; click it again to reverse the order.
tyrantAdmin.filters4: Big rounds are split into pages: use Previous and Next.
tyrantAdmin.exportBody: Download the sign-ups of the selected round:
tyrantAdmin.export1: Export CSV: one row per player, for spreadsheets or bots.
tyrantAdmin.export2: Export Excel: a formatted sheet plus a Summary sheet with the stats. Exports use each player's current profile (name, alliance, furnace, camp levels and tiers) and include only the players that match the current filters.
tyrantAdmin.deleteBody: Use the delete button on a row to remove a duplicate or test sign-up (you are asked to confirm). It removes the sign-up from this round only; the player profile is kept. Sign-ups in past rounds cannot be deleted.
tyrantAdmin.workflow1: Start a new round for the event and set a closing time.
tyrantAdmin.workflow2: Check the time windows on the Settings tab and save them.
tyrantAdmin.workflow3: Share the sign-up link in state chat.
tyrantAdmin.workflow4: Watch the stats as sign-ups arrive; remove duplicates and test entries.
tyrantAdmin.workflow5: After the closing time, filter and sort to plan rallies, then export to CSV or Excel.
tyrantAdmin.workflow6: Before the next Tyrant event, start a new round: this one stays viewable as history.
tyrantAdmin.filters5: Filters combine (all must match). Each active filter shows as a pill: tap a pill to remove it, or "Clear filters" to remove all. The filters are in the page address, so you can bookmark or share a filtered view.
tyrantAdmin.filters6: Strength (sortable) ranks joiners: for each troop type the camp FC number plus the tier, added up (FC10 camps with T11 troops everywhere = 63).
